issues.description: Override semantics silently changed; overrideCount jumped 6 to 12 against a test named 'do not run on references'
issues.detail: The old guard `if (!seen.isParent) ctx.override(...)` was removed, so override now fires unconditionally. The test assertion was bumped from 6 to 12 with no justification, even though its name claims overrides should not run on references. This is a user-visible contract change for every override author. Either restore the guard or document and changelog the new semantics.

issues.description: Developer scratchpad play.ts committed with relative source imports and console.log debugging
issues.detail: play.ts was switched from `import * as z from 'zod/v4'` to a deep relative path into `packages/zod/src/index.js` and littered with console.log scaffolding. This is a local investigation file, not part of the feature, and couples a top-level playground to internal source layout. Revert play.ts before merge.

issues.description: Property de-duplication via JSON.stringify equality is fragile and quadratic
issues.detail: Two passes delete keys when `JSON.stringify(schema[key]) === JSON.stringify(refSeen.def![key])`. Stringify equality silently depends on key order, undefined values, and non-canonical numbers, substituting serialization accident for a defined equivalence relation. It is also O(N*size) inside a nested key loop. Extract a named structural-equality helper with a stated contract, or compare by reference where possible.

issues.description: flattenRef recursion on seen.parent has no termination guard analogous to seen.ref = null
issues.detail: The ref branch sets `seen.ref = null` as a recursion sentinel, but the new parent branch calls `flattenRef(seen.parent)` with no equivalent guard. If a parent chain is revisited from multiple children or forms a cycle, behavior depends on processing order and risks stack overflow. State the well-founded order explicitly or add a visited check.

issues.description: Seen.ref and Seen.parent two-field contract is unwritten
issues.detail: Two overlapping fields now carry distinct meanings: `ref` (processor-set inheritance source) and `parent` (clone-chain ancestor), with rules like `if (!result.ref) result.ref = parent` and a sentinel `ref = null` meaning 'already flattened'. No docblock explains when they diverge, what each guarantees, or how `undefined` differs from `null`. Write the contract on the Seen interface before maintainers re-confuse the roles.

issues.description: Commit bundles three independent changes that should be separate patches
issues.detail: The diff combines (a) parent/ref tracking rework in process/finalize, (b) fileProcessor anyOf hoisting which is a user-visible JSON Schema output change, and (c) the mini ZodType flip to `{parent: true}`. Each is independently reviewable and revertable. Split into three patches so reviewers and bisect can isolate regressions.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on NEEDS-WORK. The core idea — separating processor-set `ref` from clone-chain `parent` so $ref propagation survives wrappers — is sound and fixes a real bug, but the implementation ships unwritten contracts, fragile JSON.stringify dedup, and an unguarded recursion on seen.parent. Two changes are clearly disqualifying: the scratchpad play.ts must be removed, and the silent doubling of override invocations (6 to 12) against a test named "do not run on references" must be either reverted or explicitly redocumented. The Seen two-field contract needs to be written on the type, stringify-equality replaced with a named structural helper, and the patch split into independently reviewable commits before landing.
